---
title: "Modelling backends: LightGBM and H2O"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

Every function that trains a model takes a `backend` argument:

| Backend | Install | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `"lightgbm"` (default) | `install.packages("lightgbm")` | Random hyperparameter search with cross-validation, in-process (no JVM). |
| `"h2o"` | `install.packages("h2o")` and a Java runtime | H2O AutoML: a search over several algorithms, in an H2O cluster. |

Both backends are optional dependencies (Suggests), so install at least one of
them before you train a model.

## LightGBM

The `model_config` list controls the search (see `?nm_train_lgb`):

```{r}
library(normet)

covariates <- c("ws", "wd", "temp", "RH", "atmos_pres", "blh", "tcc", "tp", "ssrd")
predictors <- c(covariates, "date_unix", "day_julian", "weekday", "hour")
df_prep <- nm_prepare_data(my1, target = "NO2", covariates = covariates)

model_lgb <- nm_train_model(
  df           = df_prep,
  target       = "value",
  covariates   = predictors,
  backend      = "lightgbm",
  model_config = list(
    n_trials = 50,                 # random-search trials (default 50)
    cv_folds = 5,                  # cross-validation folds (default 5)
    nrounds  = 1000,               # maximum boosting rounds (default 1000)
    early_stopping_rounds = 20     # default 20
  )
)
```

`num_leaves_min`/`num_leaves_max` and `learning_rate_min`/`learning_rate_max`
set the ranges searched.

## H2O AutoML

H2O runs in a separate cluster, which has to be started before training and
stopped afterwards:

```{r}
nm_init_h2o()   # n_cores = NULL uses the whole allocation; max_mem_size = "16G" etc.

model_h2o <- nm_train_model(
  df           = df_prep,
  target       = "value",
  backend      = "h2o",
  covariates   = predictors,
  model_config = list(include_algos = c("GBM", "XGBoost"), max_runtime_secs = 120)
)

nm_stop_h2o()
```

`nm_init_h2o()` retries a failed start (`max_retries`, `retry_delay`).
`nm_h2o_watchdog()` checks that the cluster is alive and restarts it if the
connection has been lost. `nm_save_model()` and
`nm_load_model()` handle both backends. With H2O, `nm_do_all_unc()` trains its
ensemble members one after another in the shared cluster, where LightGBM
trains them in parallel worker processes.

## Dependencies

| Group | Packages |
|---|---|
| Modelling backends (optional) | `lightgbm`; `h2o` (needs Java) |
| Core | `data.table`, `dplyr`, `lubridate`, `zoo`, `foreach`, `doSNOW`, `parallel` |
| Causal inference | `quadprog` |
| Data I/O | `httr2`, `jsonlite`; `ecmwfr` (optional, ERA5 from the CDS); `arrow`, `readxl` (optional, Parquet/Feather and Excel files) |
| Figures | `ggplot2`, `scales`; `patchwork` (optional, `nm_plot_embedding_diagnostics()`) |
| Caching | `digest`, `memoise` |
| Desktop GUI (optional, `gui/`) | Python 3.10+, `PySide6`, `pandas`, `matplotlib` |

The full list is in the package's
[DESCRIPTION](https://github.com/apai-sys/normet-r/blob/main/DESCRIPTION).
